sentences.zh: 上將還臨安，命楊存中宣撫江、淮、荊、襄，安節言：「存中頃以權太盛，人言籍籍，方解軍政，復授茲職，非所以全之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to return to Lin'an and ordered Yang Cunzhong to pacify the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions; Anjie said: "Cunzhong's authority was recently too great and talk was rife; he had just been relieved of military duties — to give him this post again is no way to protect him."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to return to Lin'an, he appointed Yang Cunzhong pacification commissioner for the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions. Anjie said, "Cunzhong's power had grown too great and public talk was widespread; he had only just been relieved of military command — to give him this office again is no way to protect him."

sentences.zh: 又言：「方今正當大明賞罰，乃首用劉寶、王權刻剝庸懦之人，何以激勸將士。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Just now rewards and punishments ought to be made clear — yet you first employ Liu Bao and Wang Quan, harsh men who exploit the mediocre and cowardly — how can this inspire and encourage officers and soldiers?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "This is precisely the moment to make rewards and punishments unmistakably clear, yet you begin by employing Liu Bao and Wang Quan — men who prey on the timid and incompetent. How will that stir and encourage the troops?"

sentences.zh: 上皆納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 楊存中議省江、淮州縣，安節言：「廬之合肥，和之濡須，皆昔人控扼孔道。

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong proposed reducing Jiang and Huai prefectures and counties; Anjie said: "Hefei in Lu prefecture and Ruxu in He prefecture — both were choke points of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong proposed abolishing prefectures and counties along the Jiang and Huai. Anjie said, "Hefei in Lu and Ruxu in He were both strategic choke points in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝云：『先帝東置合肥，南守襄陽，西固祁山，賊來輒破於三城之下』。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei said: 'The former emperor placed Hefei in the east, guarded Xiangyang in the south, and fortified Qishan in the west — when bandits came they were always broken below these three cities.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei said, 'My predecessor placed Hefei in the east, held Xiangyang in the south, and fortified Qishan in the west — whenever the enemy came, they were broken beneath these three strongholds.'

sentences.zh: 孫權築濡須塢，魏軍累攻不克，守將如甘寧等，常以寡制眾。

translations.literal: Sun Quan built the Ruxu fort; Wei armies repeatedly attacked without success; defending generals like Gan Ning often used the few to overcome the many.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan built the Ruxu fort, and Wei armies attacked it again and again without success; defenders such as Gan Ning often used small forces to defeat large ones.

sentences.zh: 蓋形勢之地，攻守百倍，豈有昔人得之成功，今日有之而反棄之耶？

translations.literal: These are terrain of strategic advantage — attack and defense multiplied a hundredfold — can those of old succeed by holding them while we today hold them yet abandon them?
translations.idiomatic: Such ground gives a hundredfold advantage in attack and defense — can our forebears have succeeded by holding these places while we, possessing them today, throw them away?

sentences.zh: 且濡須、巢湖之水，上接店步，下接江口，可通漕舟，乞擇將經理。」

translations.literal: Moreover the waters of Ruxu and Chaohu connect above with Dianbu and below with the river mouth — grain barges can pass — I beg that generals be chosen to manage them."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the waters of Ruxu and Chaohu link upstream with Dianbu and downstream with the river mouth, allowing grain barges to pass through. I ask that capable generals be chosen to administer them."

sentences.zh: 存中議遂格。

translations.literal: Cunzhong's proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong's proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，給廷臣筆劄陳當世事，安節請：「嚴內降之科，凡內侍省、御藥院、內東門司冗費，一切罷去。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded the throne, the court gave ministers brush and note-paper to state current affairs; Anjie requested: "Strictly enforce the rule on inner edicts; all wasteful spending of the Inner Attendant Service, Imperial Pharmacy, and Inner Eastern Gate Office — abolish it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, the court supplied ministers with writing materials to set out current affairs. Anjie requested, "Strictly enforce the prohibition on inner edicts, and abolish all redundant expenses of the Inner Attendant Service, the Imperial Pharmacy, and the Inner Eastern Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 堂除省歸吏部，長官聽辟僚屬，以清中書之務。

translations.literal: Provincial direct appointments should be restored to the Ministry of Personnel; senior officials allowed to recruit staff — to clarify the Secretariat's business.
translations.idiomatic: Direct appointments from the chief councillors' office should be returned to the Ministry of Personnel, and senior officials should be allowed to recruit their own staff, so as to lighten the Secretariat's burden.

sentences.zh: 文武蔭補，各有定制，毋令易文資。

translations.literal: Civil and military hereditary appointments each have fixed rules — do not let military officers switch to civil credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary appointments for civil and military families each have fixed regulations; do not allow military families to exchange their privilege for civil rank.

sentences.zh: 臣僚致仕遺表恩澤，不宜奏異姓，使得高貲為市。」

translations.literal: Posthumous memorial favors for retired officials — it is unfitting to grant them to unrelated surnames, enabling them to be traded at high price."
translations.idiomatic: Favors granted through posthumous memorials by retired officials should not be extended to unrelated persons, lest they become commodities sold at high price."

sentences.zh: 上嘗對大臣稱其誠實。

translations.literal: The emperor once told the ministers he was honest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised his honesty before the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 一日，因奏事面勞之曰：「近不見繳駁，有所見，但繳駁，朕無不聽。」

translations.literal: One day, while reporting business, the emperor personally praised him face to face: "Lately I have not seen memorials of protest from you — whatever you see, simply protest; I will none of it refuse to hear."
translations.idiomatic: One day, while Anjie was reporting on affairs, the emperor personally commended him: "I have not lately seen you submit protest memorials. Whatever you observe, simply protest — I will hear you out on every point."

sentences.zh: 拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 金將僕散忠義遺三省、樞密院書，論和議，乃畫定四事，詔群臣議。

translations.literal: The Jin general Pushe Zhongyi sent a letter to the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs discussing peace talks; four matters were outlined and the court ordered the ministers to debate them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Pushe Zhongyi sent a letter to the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs proposing peace talks. Four points were outlined, and the emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 安節謂：「世稱侄國，國號不加「大」字及用「再拜」二字，皆不可從。

translations.literal: Anjie said: "Calling us the nephew state, not adding 'Great' to our title, and using the two characters 'twice bow' — all unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Anjie argued, "Addressing us as a nephew state, omitting 'Great' from our dynastic title, and requiring the phrase 'twice bow' — none of these can be accepted.

sentences.zh: 海、泗、唐、鄧為淮、襄屏蔽，不可與。

translations.literal: Haizhou, Sizhou, Tangzhou, and Dengzhou are screens for the Huai and Xiang — cannot be ceded.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou, Sizhou, Tangzhou, and Dengzhou shield the Huai and Xiang frontiers and must not be surrendered.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，寧少增歲幣。

translations.literal: If it cannot be helped, better to increase the annual tribute slightly.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no alternative, it would be better to increase the annual tribute slightly.

sentences.zh: 欽宗梓宮當迎奉。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong's coffin ought to be received and enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong's coffin should be brought back and properly enshrined.

sentences.zh: 陵寢地必不肯歸我，宜每因遣使恭謁。

translations.literal: The tomb lands will surely not be returned — we ought each time we send envoys to pay reverent visit.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb grounds will surely not be returned to us; we should therefore send envoys on each occasion to pay reverent visits there.

sentences.zh: 但講好之後，當益選將厲兵，以為後圖。」

translations.literal: But after peace is made, we should more vigorously select generals and sharpen the army as preparation for the future."
translations.idiomatic: But once peace is secured, we should redouble our efforts to select able generals and train the army, keeping the long term in view."

sentences.zh: 已而請祠，得請。

translations.literal: He soon requested a sinecure and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested a sinecure post and was granted one.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人胡銓繳奏，謂：「安節太上之舊人，而陛下之老成也。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Hu Quan submitted a protest memorial, saying: "Anjie is an old associate of the Retired Emperor and a seasoned man for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Hu Quan submitted a protest memorial, saying, "Anjie is a veteran of the Retired Emperor's court and a seasoned counselor for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 漢張蒼、唐張柬之、國朝富弼、文彥博皆年八旬尚不聽其去，安節膂力未愆，有憂國心，豈宜從其引去。」

translations.literal: Zhang Cang of Han, Zhang Jianzhi of Tang, and in our dynasty Fu Bi and Wen Yanbo — all at eighty years were still not allowed to leave; Anjie's strength is not yet failing and he has a heart for the state's worries — how can we follow his request to withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang of Han, Zhang Jianzhi of Tang, and in our own dynasty Fu Bi and Wen Yanbo — all at eighty were still not permitted to retire. Anjie's vigor has not yet declined, and his concern for the state remains strong. How can we grant his request to withdraw?"

sentences.zh: 上遂留之。

translations.literal: The emperor then kept him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，權吏部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: More than a year later, acting minister of Personnel and concurrent palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he served as acting minister of Personnel and concurrent palace reader.

sentences.zh: 自是力請謝事，詔以敷文閣學士致仕。

translations.literal: From then on he vigorously begged to retire; an edict made him retired as academician of the Fuweng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he repeatedly pressed to retire, and an edict granted him retirement as academician of the Fuweng Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上曰：「卿且暫歸，旦夕召卿矣。」

translations.literal: At audience to take leave the emperor said: "You may for now return home — I shall summon you before long."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said, "Return home for now — I shall summon you again very soon."

sentences.zh: 去之日，縉紳相與歎羨，以為中興以來全名高節，鮮有其比。

translations.literal: On the day he left, court and gentry sighed in admiration together, thinking that since the Restoration, for integrity untarnished and lofty character, few could compare.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his departure, officials and gentry alike sighed in admiration, believing that since the Restoration few men of such unsullied reputation and lofty integrity could be found.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Qiandao, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Qiandao, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，贈通奉大夫，累贈開府儀同三司、少保。

translations.literal: When his posthumous memorial was received, he was posthumously given Grand Master for Court Discussion, cumulatively posthumously given Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial honors as a grand commandery, and Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial reached the throne, he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master for Court Discussion, and later cumulatively honored as Grand Preceptor with the ceremonial rank of a grand commandery and as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 安節至孝，居喪有禮。

translations.literal: Anjie was deeply filial; in mourning he observed every propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Anjie was profoundly filial and observed every proper rite while in mourning.

sentences.zh: 與兄相友愛，田業悉推與之，又以恩奏其孤子㒜。

translations.literal: He was affectionate with his elder brother, gave him all their fields and estates, and by grace memorialized his orphaned nephew Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his elder brother, turned over all their land and property to him, and used his privilege to secure an appointment for his orphaned nephew Rui.

sentences.zh: 初筮仕，未嘗求薦於人，及貴，有舉薦不令人知。

translations.literal: At first appointment he never sought recommendation from anyone; when elevated, when he recommended others he let no one know.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered office he never asked anyone for a recommendation; once he rose high, he recommended others without letting them know.

sentences.zh: 其除司農丞，或語之曰：「公是命，張侍郎致遠為中司時所薦，盍往謝之？」

translations.literal: When he was appointed vice director of the granaries bureau, someone told him: "Your appointment — Vice Minister Zhang Zhiyuan recommended you when he was chief censor — ought you not go thank him?"
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed vice director of the granaries bureau, someone said to him, "This appointment came because Vice Minister Zhang Zhiyuan recommended you when he was chief censor. Should you not go thank him?"

sentences.zh: 安節曰：「彼為朝廷薦人，豈私我耶！」

translations.literal: Anjie said: "He recommended people for the court — how was that favoring me!"
translations.idiomatic: Anjie replied, "He recommended people for the court's sake — how could that have been a personal favor to me!"

sentences.zh: 竟不往。

translations.literal: He never went.
translations.idiomatic: He never went.

sentences.zh: 薦晁公武、龔茂良可臺諫，皆稱職，二人弗知也。

translations.literal: He recommended Chao Gongwu and Gong Maoliang for remonstrance posts — both performed well — the two men never knew.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Chao Gongwu and Gong Maoliang for censorial and remonstrance posts; both served capably, and neither ever knew who had recommended him.

sentences.zh: 與秦檜忤，不出者十八年，及再起，論事終不屈，人以此服之。

translations.literal: He crossed Qin Hui and did not serve for eighteen years; when raised again he never yielded in memorializing — men admired him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen out with Qin Hui and stayed out of office for eighteen years; when he returned to service he never softened his remonstrances, and men respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷、《奏議表疏》、《周易解》。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in thirty juan, Memorials and Petitions, and Commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan, along with Memorials and Petitions and a Commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 王剛中

translations.literal: Wang Gangzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gangzhong

sentences.zh: 王剛中，字時亨，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Wang Gangzhong, styled Shiheng, was a man of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gangzhong, courtesy name Shiheng, was a native of Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 剛中博覽強記。

translations.literal: Gangzhong read widely and remembered forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong read broadly and possessed a formidable memory.

sentences.zh: 紹興十五年，進士第二人。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year of Shaoxing — second in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing he placed second in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 任某州推官，改左宣義郎。

translations.literal: He served as judicial assistant in a certain prefecture and was changed to Left Gentleman for Righteous Undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial assistant in a certain prefecture and was promoted to Left Gentleman for Righteous Undertakings.

sentences.zh: 故事當召試，秦檜怒其不詣己，授洪州教授。

translations.literal: By precedent he should have been summoned for examination — Qin Hui, angered that he did not pay court to him, gave him a professorship in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent he should have been summoned for a palace examination, but Qin Hui, angered that he had not paid court to him, instead appointed him professor in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 檜死，召見，擢秘書省校書郎，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was summoned to audience, promoted to collator in the Secretariat, and transferred to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death he was summoned to audience, promoted to collator in the Secretariat, and transferred to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 孝宗為普安郡王，剛中兼王府教授，每侍講，極陳古今治亂之故，君子小人忠佞之辨。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an, Gangzhong concurrently served as princely academy professor; each time he lectured he fully expounded causes of order and chaos through the ages and distinctions between the noble and base, the loyal and sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an, Gangzhong also served as professor in the princely academy. At each lecture he spoke at length on the causes of order and chaos through history and on how to distinguish the noble from the base, the loyal from the sycophantic.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，言：「禦敵今日先務，敵強則犯邊，弱則請盟。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat drafter and said: "Resisting the enemy is today's first task — when the enemy is strong they invade the border; when weak they seek alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat drafter and said, "Defending against the enemy is the urgent task of the day: when the enemy is strong they raid the frontier; when weak they sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 今勿計敵人之強弱，必先自治，擇將帥，搜戰士，實邊儲，備器械，國勢富強，將良士勇，請盟則為漢文帝，犯邊則為唐太宗。」

translations.literal: Now do not reckon the enemy's strength or weakness — first put the state in order: choose commanders, gather warriors, fill border stores, prepare weapons; when the nation is rich and strong, officers good and soldiers brave — seeking alliance makes one an Emperor Wen of Han, border invasion makes one an Emperor Taizong of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Do not fixate on whether the enemy is strong or weak. First put our own house in order: choose commanders, recruit soldiers, fill frontier granaries, and ready weapons. If the realm is rich and strong and our officers capable and troops brave, then seeking peace will make us like Emperor Wen of Han, and repelling invasion will make us like Emperor Taizong of Tang."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his advice.

sentences.zh: 會西蜀謀帥，上曰：「無以逾王剛中矣。」

translations.literal: When western Shu deliberated on a commander, the emperor said: "None can surpass Wang Gangzhong."
translations.idiomatic: When the court was choosing a commander for western Shu, the emperor said, "No one surpasses Wang Gangzhong."

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣待制知成都府、制置四川。

translations.literal: He was made holder of the Dragon Diagram Hall for Drafting, prefect of Chengdu, and commissioner for Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed holder of the Dragon Diagram Hall for Drafting, prefect of Chengdu, and commissioner for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 御便殿，臨遣錫金帶、象笏。

translations.literal: At the informal hall the emperor personally dispatched him, granting a gold belt and ivory tablet.
translations.idiomatic: At the informal palace hall the emperor personally saw him off, bestowing a gold belt and an ivory court tablet.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to direct academician of the Fuweng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Fuweng Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時吳璘累官閥至大帥，其下姚仲、王彥等亦建節雄一方。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Lin through accumulated offices rose to great commander; below him Yao Zhong, Wang Yan, and others also held military commissions and dominated regions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Lin had risen through successive appointments to supreme commander, while subordinates such as Yao Zhong and Wang Yan also held military commissions and ruled their regions like petty kings.

sentences.zh: 守帥以文治則玩於柔，而號令不行；

translations.literal: Prefect and commander governing by civil arts grew lax in softness and orders did not run;
translations.idiomatic: When prefects and commanders relied on civil administration they grew indulgent and weak, and their orders went unheeded;

sentences.zh: 以武競則窒於暴，而下情不通。

translations.literal: governing by martial rivalry grew choked in violence and conditions below did not reach up.
translations.idiomatic: when they competed in martial force they became brutal and oppressive, and grievances from below never reached them.

sentences.zh: 惟剛中檢身以法，示人以禮，不立崖塹，馭吏恩威並行，羽檄紛遝，從容裁決，皆中機會。

translations.literal: Only Gangzhong restrained himself by law, showed others courtesy, built no barriers, handled officials with kindness and severity together; urgent dispatches piled thick yet he calmly decided — all hitting the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong alone disciplined himself by law, treated others with courtesy, erected no barriers between himself and others, and governed his staff with both kindness and severity. Though urgent dispatches piled up, he decided each matter calmly and always to the point.

sentences.zh: 敵騎度大散關，人情洶洶。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen crossed Dasan Pass; popular sentiment was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy cavalry crossed Dasan Pass, public alarm spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 剛中跨一馬，夜馳二百里，起吳璘於帳中，責之曰：「大將與國義同休戚，臨敵安得高枕而臥？」

translations.literal: Gangzhong mounted a single horse and rode two hundred li by night, rousing Wu Lin from his tent, and rebuked him: "A great general shares weal and woe with the state — facing the enemy how can he lie on a high pillow and sleep?"
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong mounted a single horse and rode two hundred li through the night, roused Wu Lin from his tent, and rebuked him: "A great general shares life and death with the state — facing the enemy, how can you sleep at ease?"

sentences.zh: 璘大驚。

translations.literal: Lin was greatly shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 又以蠟書抵張正彥濟師。

translations.literal: He also sent a wax-sealed letter to Zhang Zhengyan to reinforce troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a wax-sealed letter urging Zhang Zhengyan to march reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 西師大集，金兵敗走。

translations.literal: Western armies massed greatly; Jin troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Western forces assembled in strength, and the Jin army was routed.

sentences.zh: 方議奏捷，剛中倍道馳還，謂其屬李燾曰：「將帥之功，吾何有焉。」

translations.literal: Just as victory was being reported, Gangzhong hurried back by forced marches and said to his aide Li Tao: "The generals' achievement — what share have I?"
translations.idiomatic: Just as a victory report was being drafted, Gangzhong raced back by forced marches and said to his aide Li Tao, "The credit belongs to the generals — what part is mine?"

sentences.zh: 燾唶曰：「身督戰而功成不居，過人遠矣。」

translations.literal: Tao clicked his tongue and said: "Personally directing battle yet not claiming the success — he surpasses others by far."
translations.idiomatic: Tao marveled and said, "To oversee the fighting in person yet refuse the credit — that puts him far above ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 已乃差擇將士，眾所推者上之朝，備統帥選。

translations.literal: Then he selected officers and soldiers; those the masses recommended he sent up to court as candidates for commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected officers and soldiers, forwarding to court those most praised by the troops as candidates for command.

sentences.zh: 又疏蜀名勝士與幕府之賢，備部使者、州刺史之佐。

translations.literal: He also memorialized eminent scholars of Shu and worthy men of the staff as candidates for provincial commissioners' and prefects' assistants.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a list of distinguished scholars of Shu and able men in his staff as candidates to serve provincial commissioners and prefects.

sentences.zh: 目使頤指，內外響應。

translations.literal: At a glance or a gesture all responded, inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: At his glance or gesture, men inside and outside the government responded as one.

sentences.zh: 諸汰遣使臣困絕不能自存，剛中以為冒刃於少壯之年，不可斥棄於既老之後，悉召詣府，有善射者復其祿秩，以禁軍闕額糧給之，其罷癃不堪事，則給以義倉米。

translations.literal: Various dismissed envoys were destitute and could not sustain themselves; Gangzhong held that men who had braved blades in youth ought not be cast off in old age — he summoned them all to the prefecture; skilled archers had ranks and salaries restored, paid from vacant quota grain of the imperial guard; those disabled and unable to serve received relief-granary rice.
translations.idiomatic: Many dismissed military envoys were destitute and could not support themselves. Gangzhong held that men who had faced swords in their prime should not be abandoned in old age. He summoned them all to the prefectural seat; skilled archers had their ranks and salaries restored and were paid from vacant imperial-guard grain quotas, while those too infirm to serve were given rice from the relief granaries.

sentences.zh: 成都萬歲池廣袤十里，溉三鄉田，歲久淤澱，剛中集三鄉夫共疏之，累土為防，上植榆柳，表以石柱，州人指曰：「王公之甘棠也。」

translations.literal: Chendu's Wansui Pool was ten li in breadth and length, irrigating three townships' fields; long years had silted it; Gangzhong assembled men of the three townships jointly to dredge it, piled earth for dikes, planted elms and willows atop, marked with stone pillars — the people of the prefecture pointed and said: "This is Lord Wang's sweet-pear tree."
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu's Wansui Pool stretched ten li in every direction and irrigated the fields of three townships, but years of silt had choked it. Gangzhong mobilized labor from all three townships to dredge it, built earthen dikes, planted elms and willows along them, and set up stone markers. The people of the prefecture pointed to the work and said, "This is Lord Wang's sweet-pear shade."

sentences.zh: 府學禮殿，東漢興平中建，後又建新學，遭時多故，日就傾圮，屬九縣繕完，悉復其舊。

translations.literal: The prefectural school's ritual hall, built in the Xingping era of Eastern Han, later a new academy was built — troubled times daily brought decay; he put the nine counties to repair and fully restored the old.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural school's ritual hall had been built in the Xingping era of Eastern Han; a new academy was later added, but years of turmoil had left both crumbling. He assigned the nine counties to repair them and fully restored their original condition.

sentences.zh: 葺諸葛武侯祠、張文定公廟，夷黃巢墓，表賢癉惡以示民。

translations.literal: He repaired Zhuge Liang's shrine and Zhang Wending's temple, levelled Huang Chao's tomb, honored the worthy and exposed the vile to show the people.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Zhuge Liang's shrine and Zhang Wending's temple, demolished Huang Chao's tomb, and honored the worthy while exposing the wicked as an example to the people.

sentences.zh: 有女巫蓄蛇為妖，殺蛇，黥之。

translations.literal: There was a witch who kept snakes for sorcery — he killed the snakes and tattooed her.
translations.idiomatic: When a witch kept snakes to work sorcery, he killed the snakes and punished her with facial tattooing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，以宮僚進左朝奉大夫，召赴闕，以足疾請祠，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, as palace staff he was advanced to Left Grand Master of Court Audience, summoned to court; with foot ailment he requested a sinecure as superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong received the abdication, Gangzhong was promoted as a palace official to Left Grand Master of Court Audience and summoned to court, but citing foot ailment he requested a sinecure as superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 歸次番陽，營圃植竹，號「竹塢」。

translations.literal: Returning he stopped at Poyang, laid out a garden and planted bamboo — called it "Bamboo Retreat."
translations.idiomatic: On his way home he stopped at Poyang, laid out a garden, planted bamboo, and called the place the Bamboo Retreat.

sentences.zh: 金犯淮，有旨趣剛中入見，陳戰守之策。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded the Huai, an edict hurried Gangzhong to audience to set forth strategies of war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded the Huai region, an edict urgently summoned Gangzhong to court to present strategies for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 除禮部尚書、直學士院兼給事中，為鹵簿使，除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，進同知院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of Rites, academician in direct attendance on the Hanlin and concurrent supervising secretary, made imperial procession commissioner, appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to vice director of the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of Rites, Hanlin academician in direct attendance, and concurrent supervising secretary; served as imperial procession commissioner; was then made academician of the Duanming Hall and signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and finally promoted to vice director of the Bureau.

sentences.zh: 剛中曰：「戰守者實事，和議者虛名，不可恃虛名害實事。」

translations.literal: Gangzhong said: "War and defense are solid business; peace talks are empty name — one must not rely on empty name to harm solid business."
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong said, "War and defense are concrete realities; peace talks are empty names — we must not sacrifice real strength for the sake of a hollow reputation for peace."

sentences.zh: 又奏四事：開屯田、省浮費、選將帥、汰冗兵。

translations.literal: He also memorialized four matters: open garrison farms, reduce floating expenses, select generals and commanders, and eliminate redundant soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted four proposals: establish frontier garrison farms, cut wasteful spending, appoint capable commanders, and trim the bloated army.

sentences.zh: 居政府，屬疾卒，年六十三，贈資政殿大學士、光祿大夫，諡「恭簡」。

translations.literal: While serving in the central government, he fell critically ill and died, aged sixty-three. Posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with posthumous title "Respectful and Simple."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the central government he fell gravely ill and died at sixty-three. The court posthumously made him Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the epithet Respectful and Simple.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，詔階、成、岷、鳳四州刺壯丁為兵，眾以為憂。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era, an edict conscripted strong young men in the four prefectures of Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng as soldiers; the people considered it worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan period, an edict ordered the conscription of able-bodied young men in the four western prefectures of Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng. The populace viewed it with alarm.

sentences.zh: 剛中建言五害罷之，免符下，民歡呼，聲震山谷。

translations.literal: Gangzhong memorialized five harms and had it abolished; when the exemption order arrived, the people shouted in joy, the sound shaking mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong memorialized on five harmful consequences and secured its repeal. When the exemption order arrived, people cheered so loudly that the valleys echoed.

sentences.zh: 比去，蜀父老遮道，有追送數百里者。

translations.literal: As he was about to leave, elders of Shu blocked the road; some followed and sent him off for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, elders of Shu blocked the road to see him off; some escorted him for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 繇布衣至公卿，無他嗜好，公退惟讀書著文為樂。

translations.literal: From commoner to high minister, he had no other indulgence; after leaving office he took only reading and writing for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from commoner to minister, he cultivated no other pleasures; after hours he read and wrote for delight alone.

sentences.zh: 有《易說》、《春秋通義》、《仙源聖紀》、《經史辨》、《漢唐史要覽》、《天人修應錄》、《東溪集》、《應齋筆錄》，凡百餘卷。

translations.literal: He had Commentaries on the Changes, Comprehensive Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, Records of Sacred Origins of the Immortal Source, Discriminations of Classics and Histories, Essential Survey of Han and Tang History, Records of Heavenly-Human Correspondence and Cultivation, Collection of Eastern Stream, and Brush Record of the Responding Study — over a hundred scrolls in total.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Commentaries on the Changes, Comprehensive Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, Records of the Immortal Source, Discriminations between Classics and Histories, Essential Survey of Han and Tang History, Records of Heavenly-Human Correspondence, Collection of Eastern Stream, and Brush Notes of the Responding Study—more than a hundred scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 李彥穎

translations.literal: Li Yanying
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanying

sentences.zh: 李彥穎，字秀叔，湖州德清人。

translations.literal: Li Yanying, style Xiushu, was a native of Deqing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanying, courtesy name Xiushu, was from Deqing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 少端重，強記覽。

translations.literal: In youth he was dignified and steady, with strong memorization and reading.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was grave and steady, with a prodigious memory.

sentences.zh: 金犯浙西，父挾家人逃避，彥穎方十歲，追不及，敵已迫其後，能趨支徑，亂流獲濟。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded western Zhe, his father took the family and fled; Yanying was just ten. Unable to catch up, with the enemy pressing from behind, he could run by side paths and cross turbulent streams to reach safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded western Zhejiang, his father fled with the family. Yanying, only ten, could not keep pace; with enemy troops close behind, he took side paths and forded rushing streams to escape.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年，擢進士第，主餘杭簿。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing, he passed the jinshi examination and served as registrar of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 18 (1148) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 守曹泳豪敚酒家業為官監，利其貲具，彥穎爭之。

translations.literal: Prefect Cao Yong forcibly seized a wine-shop family business for government supervision, coveting its assets and equipment; Yanying contested it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cao Yong forcibly seized a family wine business for state monopoly, coveting its assets and equipment; Yanying challenged the seizure.

sentences.zh: 泳怒，戒吏煆煉，不得毫髮罪。

translations.literal: Yong was angered, warning clerks to forge and torture evidence but finding not the slightest offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was furious and ordered his clerks to manufacture charges through torture, but they could not find the slightest fault.

sentences.zh: 調建德丞，改秩。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Jiande and advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Jiande and promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 時宰知其才，將處之學官，或勸使一見，彥穎恥自獻。

translations.literal: The chief minister knew his talent and was about to place him in an academic post; some urged him to pay one visit, but Yanying was ashamed to present himself.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister recognized his talent and planned to appoint him to an academic post; friends urged him to pay a courtesy visit to the minister, but Yanying was too proud to court favor.

sentences.zh: 調富陽丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 御史周操薦為御史臺主簿。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Cao recommended him as chief clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Cao recommended him for appointment as chief clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 金敗盟，張浚督師進討。

translations.literal: The Jin broke the alliance; Zhang Jun supervised the army in an advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the peace treaty, Zhang Jun took command of an offensive.

sentences.zh: 上方向浚，執政堅主和，陳良翰、周操不以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor leaned toward Jun; the chief ministers firmly advocated peace; Chen Lianghan and Zhou Cao did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Jun, but the chief ministers staunchly advocated peace. Chen Lianghan and Zhou Cao disagreed.

sentences.zh: 右正言尹穡陰符執政，薦引同己者，轉言和於上前。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Director Yin Ji secretly aligned with the chief ministers, recommending those like himself and repeatedly speaking of peace before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Director Yin Ji secretly allied with the chief ministers, promoting like-minded men and repeatedly advocating peace before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上惑之，罷督府，良翰、操相繼黜，而穡進殿中，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was misled, abolished the headquarters of the supervisor, Lianghan and Cao were successively dismissed, while Ji entered the palace and was promoted to Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was swayed. The supervisory headquarters was abolished; Lianghan and Cao were dismissed in succession, while Ji gained access to the inner palace and was promoted to Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.

sentences.zh: 一日，穡以和、戰、守叩彥穎，彥穎曰：「人所見固不同。

translations.literal: One day Ji raised the matters of peace, war, and defense with Yanying. Yanying said: "What men see is naturally different.
translations.idiomatic: One day Ji asked Yanying his views on peace, war, and defense. Yanying replied, "Men see these matters differently.

sentences.zh: 公既以和議為是，曷不明陳於上前，以身任之，事成功歸於公，不成奉身而退。

translations.literal: Since you hold peace talks correct, why not clearly state it before the emperor, take it upon yourself personally — if affairs succeed the credit returns to you; if not, withdraw by offering your person.
translations.idiomatic: If you believe peace is right, state it plainly before the emperor and stake your career on it. If it succeeds, the credit is yours; if it fails, resign and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 若欲享其利而不及其害，國事將誰倚？」

translations.literal: If you wish to enjoy its benefits but not share its harms, on whom will state affairs rely?"
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to reap its rewards without accepting its risks, upon whom will the government depend?"

sentences.zh: 穡大怒曰：「自為諫官，前後百餘奏，曷嘗及一『和』字，而臺簿有是言！」

translations.literal: Ji raged: "Since becoming remonstrance official, in over a hundred memorials before and after, when have they touched one character for 'peace' — yet this Censorate clerk speaks thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji flew into a rage. "Since I became a remonstrance official, I have submitted more than a hundred memorials—not one mentioning peace—and now this Censorate clerk dares say such things!"

sentences.zh: 自是銜彥穎，陰排之。

translations.literal: From then on he bore a grudge against Yanying and secretly worked to exclude him.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he nursed a grievance against Yanying and worked behind the scenes to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 改國子博士，權吏部郎中，以父喪去。

translations.literal: Appointed National University Erudite, acting Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Personnel; he left on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Erudite of the National University and acting Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Personnel, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 免喪，復為吏部兼皇子恭王府直講，權右史兼兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again served in Personnel, concurrently as lecturer in the Prince Gong's household, acting Right Historiographer and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned to the Ministry of Personnel, also serving as lecturer in the household of Prince Gong of Wei, acting Right Historiographer, and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 經筵，張栻講《葛覃》，言先王正家之道，因及時事，語激切，上意不懌。

translations.literal: At the Classics Lecture, Zhang Shi lectured on "Ge Tan," speaking of the ancient kings' way of rectifying the family, and by extension current affairs — his words sharp and cutting; the emperor's mood was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial lecture, Zhang Shi expounded the "Ge Tan" ode on the ancient kings' regulation of the household and turned to current affairs in blunt, forceful language. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 彥穎曰：「人臣事君，豈不能阿諛取容？

translations.literal: Yanying said: "Ministers serving their lord — can they not flatter to please?
translations.idiomatic: Yanying said, "A minister serves his sovereign—could he not simply flatter and ingratiate himself?

sentences.zh: 栻所以敢直言，正為聖明在上，得盡愛君之誠耳。

translations.literal: The reason Shi dares speak straight is precisely because a sage and enlightened sovereign is above, enabling him to exhaust his sincerity in loving the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shi dares speak plainly because Your Majesty is enlightened enough to welcome sincere devotion from his officials.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『有言逆於汝心，必求諸道。』」

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'When words oppose your heart, you must seek them in the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "When counsel runs counter to your inclination, examine whether it accords with the Way."

sentences.zh: 上意遽解，曰：「使臣下皆若此，人主應無過。」

translations.literal: The emperor's displeasure suddenly cleared; he said: "If all ministers were like this, the ruler ought to have no errors."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's annoyance vanished at once. "If all my ministers were like this," he said, "I would seldom err."

sentences.zh: 立皇太子，兼左諭德。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was established, he concurrently served as Left Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was designated, Yanying was also appointed Left Tutor.

sentences.zh: 首論建置宮僚，以為詹事於東宮內外無所不當省，事須白詹事而後行。

translations.literal: He first discussed establishing palace staff, holding that the Grand Tutor of the Eastern Palace should oversee all matters inside and outside; affairs must be reported to the Grand Tutor before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: He first addressed the organization of the crown prince's staff, arguing that the Grand Tutor should supervise all affairs within and beyond the Eastern Palace, with nothing undertaken until reported to him.

sentences.zh: 司馬光論皇太子講讀官有奏疏，錄以進。

translations.literal: Sima Guang's memorial on the crown prince's lecture and reading officials was copied and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He transcribed and submitted Sima Guang's memorial on the crown prince's tutors and readers.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，行之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 皇太子尹臨安，兼判官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the crown prince governed Lin'an, he concurrently served as administrative judge and Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was put in charge of Lin'an, Yanying also served as his administrative judge and Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張說再登樞筦，彥穎論：「說無寸長，去年驟躋宥府，物議沸騰。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue again entered the pivot of power; Yanying argued: "Yue has not a span of merit; last year he suddenly ascended to the Forbidden Treasury of the Palace, public opinion boiling over.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was again appointed to the Military Affairs Commission, Yanying protested: "Yue possesses not a shred of talent. Last year he was suddenly elevated to the highest council of state, and public opinion was outraged.

sentences.zh: 今此命復出，中外駭然。

translations.literal: Now this appointment comes again; inside and outside are startled.
translations.idiomatic: Now this appointment has been issued again, and shock runs through court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 臣恐六軍解體，人心不服。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears the Six Armies will disintegrate and hearts will not submit."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the Six Armies will lose cohesion and the people will refuse to accept it."

sentences.zh: 未幾，權禮部侍郎兼侍講，因言：「士習委靡，不然則矯激，宜擇篤實鯁亮者用之。」

translations.literal: Before long, acting Vice Minister of Rites and concurrent lecturer, he said: "Scholarly practice is lax and weak, or else it is strident and extreme — one should select those of solid character and upright candor to employ."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as acting Vice Minister of Rites and imperial lecturer, he said, "Scholarly culture has grown either lax or shrilly extreme. We should appoint men of solid character and uncompromising integrity."

sentences.zh: 升詹事，見上，言：「皇太子尹臨安已久，雖欲更嘗民事，然非便，宜一意講學。」

translations.literal: Promoted to Grand Tutor, on audience with the emperor he said: "The crown prince has governed Lin'an for long; though one may wish him to taste further civil affairs, it is not convenient — he should devote himself solely to study."
translations.idiomatic: On promotion to Grand Tutor, he told the emperor, "The crown prince has governed Lin'an long enough. Though one might wish him more practical experience, this is not the right course; he should concentrate on his studies."

sentences.zh: 他日以言於上者告太子，趣草奏辭尹事，三辭乃免。

translations.literal: Another day he reported to the crown prince what he had said to the emperor, urging a draft memorial resigning the governorship; after three refusals he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told the crown prince what he had said to the emperor and urged him to draft a memorial resigning the governorship. After three petitions the appointment was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 兼吏部侍郎，權尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel, acting Minister and concurrent reader.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Vice Minister of Personnel, acting Minister of Personnel, and imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 月食淫雨，言：「甲申歲以淫雨求言，今十年矣，中間非無水旱，而不聞求言之詔，豈以言多沽激，厭之耶？

translations.literal: During a lunar eclipse amid heavy rain, he said: "In the jiashen year, because of heavy rain an edict sought remonstrance — now ten years have passed; in between there have been floods and droughts, yet no edict seeking remonstrance is heard — is it because remonstrances were too many and inflammatory, so one has grown weary?
translations.idiomatic: During a lunar eclipse amid torrential rains, he said, "In the jiashen year the court solicited remonstrance because of flooding. Ten years have passed; floods and droughts have struck again, yet no such edict has been issued. Have you grown weary because so many memorials were merely inflammatory?

sentences.zh: 比欺蔽成風，侍從、臺諫猶慎嘿，況其他乎？

translations.literal: Recently deception and concealment have become custom; attendant officials and remonstrance censors still guard silence — how much more others?
translations.idiomatic: Deception and cover-up have become habitual; even attendants and censors keep silent—what of lesser officials?

sentences.zh: 陰沴之興，未必不由此。」

translations.literal: The rise of yin maleficence may not fail to stem from this."
translations.idiomatic: Such celestial portents may well arise from this."

sentences.zh: 時廷臣多以中批斥去，彥穎又言：「臣下有過，宜顯逐之，使中外知獲罪之由以為戒。

translations.literal: At that time many court ministers were dismissed through confidential palace edicts; Yanying also said: "If subordinates have faults, they should be openly expelled so that inside and outside know the cause of their punishment as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials had been dismissed by secret palace edict; Yanying added, "When a minister errs, dismiss him openly so that the cause of his disgrace may serve as a warning throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今譖毀潛行，斥命中出，在廷莫測其故，將恐陰邪得伸，善類喪氣，非盛世事也。」

translations.literal: Now slander proceeds in secret, dismissals ordered from the palace — those at court cannot fathom the cause; I fear the sinister and depraved will extend themselves and good men lose spirit — this is no business of a flourishing age."
translations.idiomatic: Now slander circulates in secret and dismissals arrive by palace edict. No one at court knows why. I fear the wicked will prevail and good men lose heart—this is unworthy of an age of flourishing governance."

sentences.zh: 除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 接送金賀正使，言兩淮兵備城築及裁減接送浮費甚悉，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Escorting and receiving the Jin envoy for New Year's congratulations, he spoke at length on the two Huai military preparations, fortifications, and cutting floating expenses for escort and reception; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the Jin envoy for New Year's observances, he presented detailed proposals on military preparedness and fortifications in the two Huai regions and on reducing wasteful escort expenses. The emperor approved them warmly.

sentences.zh: 十二月，除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Accomplishment and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Accomplishment and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年閏九月，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year, ninth month (intercalary), Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month of the second year of his reign, he was made Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 金使至，上遣王抃諭金使稍變受書舊禮，議久不決。

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy arrived, the emperor dispatched Wang Bian to inform the Jin envoy of slightly changing the old ritual of receiving the letter; deliberation long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: When a Jin envoy arrived, the emperor sent Wang Bian to propose a slight modification to the old ceremony for receiving the imperial letter of state. Deliberations dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 彥穎曰：「須於國體無損而事可濟，乃善，若如去年張子顏之行，不但無益。」

translations.literal: Yanying said: "It must not harm the dignity of the state and affairs must be achievable — only then is it good; if like last year's mission of Zhang Ziyan, not only no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Yanying said, "Any change must preserve the dignity of the state and still be achievable. Last year's mission led by Zhang Ziyan accomplished nothing at all."

sentences.zh: 時左司諫湯邦彥新進，冀僥倖集事，自許立節。

translations.literal: At that time Left Remonstrance of the Secretariat Tang Bangyan was newly risen, hoping by lucky chance to gather achievements, promising himself to establish rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bangyan, a newly appointed remonstrance official of the Secretariat Chancellery, hoped to seize his chance for glory and styled himself a man of principle.

sentences.zh: 彥穎言邦彥輕脫，必誤國。

translations.literal: Yanying said Bangyan was frivolous and rash, certain to harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yanying said Bangyan was rash and irresponsible and would surely harm the country.

sentences.zh: 他日，對便殿，上復語及之。

translations.literal: Another day, at audience in the Convenient Hall, the emperor again spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, at an audience in the Convenient Hall, the emperor raised the matter again.

sentences.zh: 顏穎欲進說，上色動，宰相亟引退。

translations.literal: Yanying wished to advance his counsel; the emperor's countenance changed; the chief councilor hastily withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yanying tried to remonstrate further, but the emperor's expression darkened and the chief councilor quickly drew him away.

sentences.zh: 遂以邦彥為申議國信使，且命福建造海船，起兩淮民兵赴合肥訓練，並詔諸軍飭戎備，中外騷然。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bangyan was made envoy of letter and negotiation to the Jin, and also ordered Fujian to build sea vessels, called up militia from the two Huai to Hefei for training, and edicts to all armies to prepare military readiness — inside and outside were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan was appointed chief negotiator to the Jin, Fujian was ordered to build warships, militia from the two Huai were conscripted for training at Hefei, and every army was put on alert. Alarm spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 彥穎復言：「兩淮州縣去合肥，遠者千餘里，近亦二三百里。

translations.literal: Yanying again said: "Prefectures and counties of the two Huai from Hefei — the distant more than a thousand li, the near two or three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Yanying remonstrated again: "Prefectures and counties of the two Huai lie far from Hefei—more than a thousand li at the farthest, two or three hundred even at the nearest.

sentences.zh: 令民戶三丁起其二，限三月而罷，事未集，民先失業矣。」

translations.literal: Ordering three males per household to furnish two, limited to three months then dismissed — affairs not yet gathered, the people first lose their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: To conscript two of every three able-bodied men for only three months' training will ruin livelihoods long before any army is formed."

sentences.zh: 上作色曰：「卿欲盡撤邊備耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor showed anger: "Do you wish to withdraw all border defenses?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed with anger. "Do you mean to dismantle all our frontier defenses?"

sentences.zh: 彥穎曰：「今不得已，令三百里內，家起一丁詣合肥，三百里外，就州縣訓習，日增給錢米，限一月罷，庶不大擾。」

translations.literal: Yanying said: "Now as a last resort, within three hundred li let each household send one man to Hefei; beyond three hundred li let them drill at prefectures and counties, daily increasing rations of money and grain, limited to one month then dismissed — perhaps not greatly disturbing."
translations.idiomatic: Yanying replied, "As a compromise, households within three hundred li might send one man each to Hefei; beyond that distance men should drill locally, with daily grain and pay for one month only—that would cause far less disruption."

sentences.zh: 翌日，復執奏，從之。

translations.literal: The next day he again firmly memorialized; it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pressed his memorial again, and the emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 洎邦彥辱命而還，彥穎論其罪，貶新州。

translations.literal: When Bangyan returned after disgracing the mission, Yanying argued his guilt; he was demoted to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangyan returned in disgrace, Yanying indicted him; he was exiled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥穎在東府三歲，實攝相事，內降繳回甚多。

translations.literal: Yanying was in the Eastern Secretariat three years, in fact handling chancellor affairs; many confidential palace edicts were returned unapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanying served three years in the Eastern Secretariat, effectively acting as chief councilor, and returned many unauthorized palace edicts without executing them.

sentences.zh: 內侍白劄籍名造器械並犒師，降旨發左藏、封樁諸庫錢，動億萬計。

translations.literal: Palace attendants sent plain memorials listing names to manufacture weapons and reward troops; decrees went down to disburse funds from the Left Storehouse and sealed-reserve treasuries — reaching hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants submitted informal lists naming men to be rewarded and weapons to be forged, and palace orders went out to disburse funds from the Left Storehouse and sealed reserve treasuries—sums running into tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 彥穎疏歲中經費以進，因言：「虞允文建此庫以備邊，故曰『封樁』，陛下方有意恢復，苟用之不節，徒啟他日妄費，失封樁初意。」

translations.literal: Yanying submitted a memorial on annual expenditures, saying: "Yu Yunwen established this treasury to prepare the border, hence called 'sealed reserve'; Your Majesty just now intends recovery — if use is without restraint, it merely invites future reckless spending, losing the original intent of the sealed reserve."
translations.idiomatic: Yanying submitted a budget of annual expenditures and argued, "Yu Yunwen created these reserves for frontier defense—hence the name 'sealed reserve.' Your Majesty aspires to recover lost territory; if we spend recklessly now, we invite future waste and betray the treasury's purpose."

sentences.zh: 上矍然曰：「卿言是，朕失之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor started awake and said: "Your words are correct; I have been at fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started as if awakened. "You are right," he said. "I have erred."

sentences.zh: 自是絕不支。

translations.literal: From then on he never disbursed from them.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward, no further disbursements were made from those reserves.

sentences.zh: 墜馬在告，力求去，以資政殿學士知紹興府，勤約有惠政。

translations.literal: Having fallen from a horse he was on sick leave; he forcefully sought departure, serving as Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and prefect of Shaoxing — frugal and restrained with benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: After a fall from his horse he took sick leave and pleaded repeatedly to resign, eventually serving as Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and prefect of Shaoxing, where his frugal and conscientious rule benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 提舉洞霄宮，復參知政事，病羸，艱拜起，力辭，上曰：「老者不以筋力為禮，孟享禮繁，特免卿。」

translations.literal: Summoned to direct affairs at the Tongxiao Palace, again Vice Grand Councilor — ill and weak, bowing and rising with difficulty, he forcefully declined; the emperor said: "The aged need not observe ritual by muscular strength; the spring rites for the ancestors are elaborate — I specially exempt you."
translations.idiomatic: After appointment to supervise the Tongxiao Palace, he was again made Vice Grand Councilor. Frail and barely able to bow, he pleaded to be excused. The emperor said, "The old are not judged by physical strength. The spring ancestral rites are arduous—I exempt you from them."

sentences.zh: 諫官論其子毆人至死，奉祠鐫秩。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials argued his son beat a man to death; he was given a temple sinecure and his rank was engraved downward.
translations.idiomatic: Censors indicted his son for beating a man to death. Yanying was given a temple appointment and his rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 起知婺州，禁民屠牛，捐屬縣稅十三萬三千緡。

translations.literal: Reappointed prefect of Wuzhou, forbade the people from slaughtering cattle, donated 133,000 strings of tax from subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed prefect of Wuzhou, he banned the slaughter of cattle by commoners and remitted 133,000 strings of copper in taxes owed by subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 復知紹興府，進資政殿大學士，再奉祠，進觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: Again prefect of Shaoxing, promoted to Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance, again given temple sinecure, promoted to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as prefect of Shaoxing, was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance, received another temple appointment, and was made Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 1 (1190) he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 家居凡十載，自奉澹約，食才米數合。

translations.literal: At home for ten years in all, his self-support plain and restrained, eating only several gō of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for ten years, maintaining a spare existence on no more than a few gō of rice a day.

sentences.zh: 室無姬媵，蕭然永日，與州縣了不相聞。

translations.literal: The house without concubines or attendants; desolate through long days, having nothing to do with prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no concubines; his days passed in austere solitude, and he had no contact with local officials.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十一，贈少保，諡「忠文」。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-one, posthumously granted Junior Guardian, with posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one. The court posthumously made him Junior Guardian with the epithet Loyal and Literary.

sentences.zh: 子沐，慶元中，與一時臺諫排趙汝愚，善類一空，公論醜之。

translations.literal: His son Mu, during the Qingyuan era, with remonstrance censors of the time expelled Zhao Ruyu; good men were emptied at once, public opinion found it shameful.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mu, during the Qingyuan persecution, joined the censorial faction that drove out Zhao Ruyu and purged the upright from office—a deed widely condemned.

sentences.zh: 范成大

translations.literal: Fan Chengda
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda

sentences.zh: 起知處州。

translations.literal: He was raised and appointed prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陛對，論力之所及者三，曰日力，曰國力，曰人力，今盡以虛文耗之，上嘉納。

translations.literal: At court audience he discussed three things force could reach: day force, state force, and human force — now all are exhausted by empty documents; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At his formal audience he identified three kinds of national capacity—daily labor, fiscal resources, and manpower—all now squandered on empty paperwork. The emperor praised his analysis and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 處民以爭役囂訟，成大為創義役，隨家貧富輸金買田，助當役者，甲乙輪第至二十年，民便之。

translations.literal: The people of Chuzhou clamored in lawsuits over corvée disputes; Chengda created righteousness-corvée: according to each family's wealth and poverty contribute gold to buy fields, aiding those serving corvée; ranked in jia and yi rotation for twenty years — the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chuzhou quarreled constantly over corvée obligations. Chengda devised a "righteous corvée" system: households contributed according to wealth to purchase communal land, helping those currently on duty, with turns rotating over twenty years. The people welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 其後入奏，言及此，詔頒其法于諸路。

translations.literal: Later on entering court to report, he spoke of this; an edict promulgated his method to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When he later reported to court, the emperor ordered his system promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 處多山田，梁天監中，詹、南二司馬作通濟堰在松陽、遂昌之間，激溪水四十里，溉田二十萬畝。

translations.literal: Chuzhou had many mountain fields; in Tianjian of Liang, the two Marshals Zhan and Nan made the Tongji Weir between Songyang and Suichang, channeling stream water forty li, irrigating two hundred thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou's terraced farmlands depended on the Tongji Weir, built in Liang Tianjian by the two marshals Zhan and Nan between Songyang and Suichang, which diverted streamwater for forty li and irrigated two hundred thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 堰歲久壞，成大訪故跡，疊石築防，置堤閘四十九所，立水則，上中下溉灌有序，民食其利。

translations.literal: The weir long broken through years, Chengda traced the old traces, piled stone to build barriers, set forty-nine embankment gates, established water gauges — upper, middle, and lower irrigation in order; the people ate its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: After years of decay Chengda traced the old works, rebuilt the stonework, installed forty-nine sluice gates, set watermarks for staged irrigation, and restored orderly distribution of water from upper to lower reaches. The people reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 除禮部員外郎兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Appointed Outer Gentleman of Rites and concurrent lecturer at the Hall for Venerating Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and lecturer at the Hall for Venerating Governance.

sentences.zh: 乾道《令》以絹計贓，估價輕而論罪重，成大奏：「承平時絹匹不及千錢，而估價過倍。

translations.literal: The Qiandao Statutes calculated stolen goods by silk; valuation was light but crime judgment heavy; Chengda memorialized: "In peaceful times a bolt of silk did not reach a thousand cash, yet valuation exceeded double.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qiandao statutes, theft was assessed by the value of silk bolts—undervalued for the goods but inflated for sentencing. Chengda memorialized: "In peaceful times a bolt sold for less than a thousand cash, yet the statutory valuation was more than double that.

sentences.zh: 紹興初年遞增五分，為錢三千足。

translations.literal: In early Shaoxing it increased by five parts in succession to three thousand cash full.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shaoxing the assessed rate rose in increments of five percent until it reached three thousand cash per bolt.

sentences.zh: 今絹實貴，當倍時直。」

translations.literal: Now silk is truly expensive — it should double the current price."
translations.idiomatic: Silk is far costlier today; the valuation should be doubled to reflect actual prices."

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「是陷民深文。」

translations.literal: The emperor startled: "This traps the people in severe statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished. "That would trap common people under harsh penalties."

sentences.zh: 遂增為四千，而刑輕矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was increased to four thousand, and punishments grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: The valuation was raised to four thousand cash, and sentences became correspondingly lighter.

sentences.zh: 隆興再講和，失定受書之禮，上嘗悔之。

translations.literal: In Longxing peace was discussed again; the fixed ritual of receiving the letter was lost; the emperor once regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: During the renewed peace talks of the Longxing era, the established ceremony for receiving the imperial letter was abandoned, to the emperor's lasting regret.

sentences.zh: 遷成大起居郎，假資政殿大學士，充金祈請國信使。

translations.literal: Chengda was transferred to Attendant of Affairs, temporarily granted Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance, serving as chief envoy to the Jin requesting letter of state.
translations.idiomatic: Chengda was promoted to Attendant of Affairs and provisionally given the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance as chief envoy to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 國書專求陵寢，蓋泛使也。

translations.literal: The letter of state solely sought imperial tombs — in effect a general envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The formal letter sought only access to the imperial tombs—in effect a goodwill mission without diplomatic substance.

sentences.zh: 上面諭受書事，成大乞併載書中，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor personally instructed on the matter of receiving the letter; Chengda requested it be included together in the letter; not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally instructed him on the ceremony for receiving the letter of state. Chengda asked that the demand be included in the formal missive, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 金迎使者慕成大名，至求巾幘效之。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy who came to welcome him admired Chengda's great fame and even asked for a headcloth to imitate his style.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy who came to welcome him admired Chengda's great fame and even asked for a headcloth to imitate his style.

sentences.zh: 至燕山，密草奏，具言受書式，懷之入。

translations.literal: At Yan Mountain he secretly drafted a memorial setting forth the form for receiving the letter of credence and carried it hidden on his person when he entered.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan Mountain he secretly drafted a memorial setting forth the form for receiving the letter of credence and carried it hidden on his person when he entered.

sentences.zh: 初進國書，詞氣慷慨，金君臣方傾聽，成大忽奏曰：「兩朝既為叔侄，而受書禮未稱，臣有疏。」

translations.literal: When he first presented the state letter, his language was impassioned; as the Jin ruler and ministers were listening intently, Chengda suddenly memorialized: "The two courts are already uncle and nephew, yet the rites for receiving the letter are not fitting — your servant has a memorial."
translations.idiomatic: When he first presented the state letter, his language was impassioned; as the Jin ruler and ministers were listening intently, Chengda suddenly memorialized, "The two courts are already uncle and nephew, yet the rites for receiving the letter are not fitting — your servant has a memorial."

sentences.zh: 搢笏出之。

translations.literal: He took his memorial tablet from his girdle and produced it.
translations.idiomatic: He took his memorial tablet from his girdle and produced it.

sentences.zh: 金主大駭，曰：「此豈獻書處耶？」

translations.literal: The Jin ruler was greatly alarmed and said: "Is this the place to present a memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler was greatly alarmed and said, "Is this the place to present a memorial?"

sentences.zh: 左右以笏標起之，成大屹不動，必欲書達。

translations.literal: Attendants used their tablets to mark him and raise him up, but Chengda stood firm and unmoved, insisting that the memorial be received.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants used their tablets to mark him and raise him up, but Chengda stood firm and unmoved, insisting that the memorial be received.

sentences.zh: 既而歸館所，金主遣伴使宣旨取奏。

translations.literal: Afterward he returned to the guest lodge; the Jin ruler sent an accompanying envoy to announce the imperial command and take the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he returned to the guest lodge; the Jin ruler sent an accompanying envoy to announce the imperial command and take the memorial.

sentences.zh: 成大之未起也，金庭紛然，太子欲殺成大，越王止之，竟得全節而歸。

translations.literal: Before Chengda rose, the Jin court was in an uproar; the crown prince wished to kill Chengda, but the Prince of Yue stopped him — in the end he preserved his integrity and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chengda rose, the Jin court was in an uproar; the crown prince wished to kill Chengda, but the Prince of Yue stopped him — in the end he preserved his integrity and returned.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed drafting companion at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 初，上書崔寔《政論》賜輔臣，成大奏曰：「御書《政論》，意在飭綱紀，振積敝。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent Cui Shi's Political Treatise to the chief ministers as a gift; Chengda memorialized: "The imperial copy of the Political Treatise aims to tighten discipline and revive long-standing abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent Cui Shi's Political Treatise to the chief ministers as a gift; Chengda memorialized, "The imperial copy of the Political Treatise aims to tighten discipline and revive long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 而近日大理議刑，遞加一等，此非以嚴致平，乃酷也。」

translations.literal: Yet recently the Court of Judicial Review in sentencing has added a grade of punishment in succession — this is not governing through severity toward peace but cruelty."
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently the Court of Judicial Review in sentencing has added a grade of punishment in succession — this is not governing through severity toward peace but cruelty."

sentences.zh: 上稱為知言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him as speaking to the point.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him as speaking to the point.

sentences.zh: 張說除簽書樞密院事，成大當制，留詞頭七日不下，又上疏言之，說命竟寢。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shuo was appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, Chengda as drafter held back the appointment text for seven days without issuing it, and again submitted a memorial on the matter — Shuo's appointment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo was appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, Chengda as drafter held back the appointment text for seven days without issuing it, and again submitted a memorial on the matter — Shuo's appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 知靜江府。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 廣西窘匱，專藉鹽利，漕臣盡取之，於是屬邑有增價抑配之敝，詔復行鈔鹽，漕司拘鈔錢均給所部，而錢不時至。

translations.literal: Guangxi was straitened and relied solely on salt profits; transport officials took all of it, so subordinate counties suffered the abuse of price hikes and forced allocation; an edict restored the salt certificate system, and the transport bureau was to distribute certificate funds evenly to its jurisdictions — but the money did not arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi was straitened and relied solely on salt profits; transport officials took all of it, so subordinate counties suffered the abuse of price hikes and forced allocation; an edict restored the salt certificate system, and the transport bureau was to distribute certificate funds evenly to its jurisdictions — but the money did not arrive on time.

sentences.zh: 成大入境，曰：「利害有大於此乎？」

translations.literal: On entering his jurisdiction Chengda said: "Is there any harm greater than this?"
translations.idiomatic: On entering his jurisdiction Chengda said, "Is there any harm greater than this?"

sentences.zh: 奏疏謂：「能裁抑漕司強取之數，以寬郡縣，則科抑可禁。」

translations.literal: In his memorial he said: "If the transport bureau's forcible exactions can be cut back to ease the prefectures and counties, then forced levies can be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he said, "If the transport bureau's forcible exactions can be cut back to ease the prefectures and counties, then forced levies can be stopped."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 數年，廣州鹽商上書，乞復令客販，宰相可其說，大出銀錢助之。

translations.literal: After several years Guangzhou salt merchants petitioned to restore the old rule allowing traveling merchants to sell; the chief councillor approved and advanced large sums in silver to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Guangzhou salt merchants petitioned to restore the old rule allowing traveling merchants to sell; the chief councillor approved and advanced large sums in silver to assist them.

sentences.zh: 人多以為非，下有司議，卒不易成大說。

translations.literal: Many thought this wrong; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for discussion, and in the end Chengda's view was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Many thought this wrong; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for discussion, and in the end Chengda's view was not changed.

sentences.zh: 舊法馬以四尺三寸為限，詔加至四寸以上，成大謂互市四十年，不宜驟改。

translations.literal: Under the old law horses were limited to four feet three inches in height; an edict raised the minimum to four feet and above — Chengda said that in forty years of border trade this should not be changed abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law horses were limited to four feet three inches in height; an edict raised the minimum to four feet and above — Chengda said that in forty years of border trade this should not be changed abruptly.

sentences.zh: 除敷文閣待制、四川制置使，疏言：「吐蕃、青羌兩犯黎州，而奴兒結、蕃列等尤桀黠，輕視中國。

translations.literal: Appointed attendant of the Filled Writings Hall and Sichuan military commissioner; in his memorial he said: "Tibetans and Qing Qiang have twice raided Lizhou, and Nu'erjie, Fanlie, and others are especially fierce and look down on China.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed attendant of the Filled Writings Hall and Sichuan military commissioner; in his memorial he said, "Tibetans and Qing Qiang have twice raided Lizhou, and Nu'erjie, Fanlie, and others are especially fierce and look down on China.

sentences.zh: 臣當教閱將兵，外修堡砦，仍講明教閱團結之法，使人自為戰，三者非財不可。」

translations.literal: Your servant will train and review troops, repair fortresses on the outer line, and clarify methods of training and militia organization so that men fight for themselves — all three require funds."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant will train and review troops, repair fortresses on the outer line, and clarify methods of training and militia organization so that men fight for themselves — all three require funds."

sentences.zh: 上賜度牒錢四十萬緡。

translations.literal: The emperor granted forty thousand strings in ordination certificate funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted forty thousand strings in ordination certificate funds.

sentences.zh: 成大謂西南諸邊，黎為要地，增戰兵五千，奏置路分都監。

translations.literal: Chengda held that among the southwestern borders Li prefecture was the key point; he added five thousand battle troops and memorialized to establish circuit-level supervisory commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Chengda held that among the southwestern borders Li prefecture was the key point; he added five thousand battle troops and memorialized to establish circuit-level supervisory commanders.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇之路十有八，悉築柵分戍。

translations.literal: There were eighteen routes by which Tibetans invaded; he built stockades and garrisoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: There were eighteen routes by which Tibetans invaded; he built stockades and garrisoned them all.

sentences.zh: 奴兒結擾安靜砦，發飛山軍千人赴之，料其三日必遁，已而果然。

translations.literal: When Nu'erjie harassed Anjing stockade, he sent a thousand men of the Flying Mountain Army — judging they would withdraw within three days, and so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: When Nu'erjie harassed Anjing stockade, he sent a thousand men of the Flying Mountain Army — judging they would withdraw within three days, and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 白水砦將王文才私娶蠻女，常導之寇邊，成大重賞檄群蠻使相疑貳，俄禽文才以獻，即斬之。

translations.literal: Wang Wencai, commander of Baishui stockade, privately married a barbarian woman and often guided raids on the border; Chengda offered heavy rewards and sent proclamations to the various tribes to sow mutual suspicion — soon Wencai was captured and presented, and was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wencai, commander of Baishui stockade, privately married a barbarian woman and often guided raids on the border; Chengda offered heavy rewards and sent proclamations to the various tribes to sow mutual suspicion — soon Wencai was captured and presented, and was beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 蜀北邊舊有義士三萬，本民兵也，監司、郡守雜役之，都統司又俾與大軍更戍，成大力言其不可，詔遵舊法。

translations.literal: On the northern border of Shu there were formerly thirty thousand righteous warriors, originally militia; supervisory commissioners and prefects mixed them in miscellaneous labor, and the supreme command also made them rotate guard duty with the main army — Chengda spoke forcefully that this must not be; an edict followed the old law.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern border of Shu there were formerly thirty thousand righteous warriors, originally militia; supervisory commissioners and prefects mixed them in miscellaneous labor, and the supreme command also made them rotate guard duty with the main army — Chengda spoke forcefully that this must not be; an edict followed the old law.

sentences.zh: 蜀知名士孫松壽年六十餘，樊漢廣甫五十九，皆掛冠不仕，表其節，詔召之，皆不起，蜀士由是歸心。

translations.literal: The renowned Shu scholars Sun Shoushou, over sixty, and Fan Hanguang, just fifty-nine, had both hung up their caps and would not serve — he memorialized their integrity; an edict summoned them, but neither came — Shu scholars thereafter gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The renowned Shu scholars Sun Shoushou, over sixty, and Fan Hanguang, just fifty-nine, had both hung up their caps and would not serve — he memorialized their integrity; an edict summoned them, but neither came — Shu scholars thereafter gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 凡人才可用者，悉致幕下，用所長，不拘小節，其傑然者露章薦之，往往顯於朝，位至二府。

translations.literal: Whatever talent could be used he brought into his staff, employing their strengths without fussing over small faults; the outstanding he recommended by open memorial, and many rose to prominence at court, some reaching the two chief councils.
